idea.why: Decomposition matches the brief: two analyst agents each owning one source, an editor agent that merges and cross-references the two digests into prioritised cards, then presentation and delivery as separate steps.

structure.why: Node types mostly right: gmailTool/googleCalendarTool as ai_tool sub-nodes, one shared model, and the html node with generateHtmlTemplate rather than a Code node hand-rolling markup. The misfit is using an LLM tool call for what is a deterministic fetch.

connections.why: The two independent branches are serialised: Calendar Agent waits on Email Triage Agent for no data reason, since the editor pulls both digests by reference anyway.

answer.why: End to end it delivers, but the style block sits after the closing html tag and CSS grid is unreliable in mail clients, so the dashboard will often land as plain stacked cards.

appraisal: A well-conceived briefing crew: two source-specialist agents with tightly scoped tools, an editor agent that merges and cross-references rather than concatenates, and a purpose-built HTML node doing the chrome so the model only emits a fragment. The prompts are unusually disciplined, with explicit buckets, anti-hallucination clauses and empty-state text, which is what makes the output survive a quiet inbox. The clear weak spot is the wiring: chaining the email agent into the calendar agent creates a dependency that does not exist, serialising two unrelated fetches and coupling their failure modes. Secondary issue is the delivery medium: the styling is written for a browser but shipped through Gmail. A knowledgeable user would fan the trigger out to both analysts and rejoin at a Merge, then inline the critical CSS or publish the page behind a webhook.
